# SHA-256 over the ANCHORED REGION -- the line the anchor sits on plus every
# following line indented more deeply than it, which is the block that label
# opens. `bin/check-conformance-drift` re-measures and lists what moved, so a
# conformance sweep can re-judge the rows whose evidence changed instead of
# PROVENANCE IS PER ROW, which is what makes a PARTIAL re-judgement
# recordable (K-1552). `ref` is the commit that row's fingerprint was
# measured at -- or `dirty` when the cited file differed from HEAD then, or
# `unknown` when git could not answer. `--record --only <scope>` re-measures
# the scope, stamps those rows at head and leaves every other row
# byte-identical, so this file can say «these were re-judged then, the rest
# are still pending» instead of forcing all-or-nothing. The stamp below is
# the LAST record operation, not a claim about every row.
# THIS FILE IS A SWEEP'S WATERMARK, NOT A LOCK. Re-record it when a sweep has
# RE-JUDGED the drifted rows -- never to make a run quiet. Nothing in CI reads
# these fingerprints AS DRIFT: drift is the normal state between sweeps and a
# gate on it would have to be switched off the day it was added. What CI does
# run is `bin/check-conformance-drift --check`, which asks only whether this
# file is one its own generator could have written -- row form and order, this
# header, and that every fingerprint re-measures to its recorded value at the
# commit ITS OWN ROW names. That never looks at head, so it cannot push the
# watermark forward. Repair a drifted header with --reheader, which re-renders
# this block and touches no fingerprint.
